blocks.text: Hypothesis testing uses several important concepts to make correct decisions. Each concept has a specific role in testing. Understanding them avoids confusion. They guide acceptance or rejection of hypotheses. These concepts are used together. Proper knowledge improves accuracy. They are applied in data analysis. Learning these concepts is essential.
Test Statistics

Test statistics are numerical values. They are calculated from sample data. These values summarize data behavior. Test statistics help compare results and support decisions. They show how far results are from expectations. Different tests use different statistics. Examples include t-value and chi-square value.

Critical Region

The critical region is a range of values. If test statistics fall in this region, the null hypothesis is rejected. It is defined before testing. The region depends on the significance level. It shows extreme outcomes. Critical regions help make decisions. They reduce uncertainty. Graphs often show critical regions. Understanding this concept is important.
Significance Level

The significance level shows risk of error. It is written as alpha. Common values include 0.05. It defines how strict a test is. Lower values mean stricter testing. It is chosen before analysis. Significance level controls false results and affects decision-making. Proper choice improves reliability.
P-value and its Importance

The p-value shows the strength of evidence against the null hypothesis. It measures the probability of getting the observed results, or more extreme results, if the null hypothesis is true. A small p-value supports the rejection of the null hypothesis because it suggests that the result is unlikely to have occurred by chance. The p-value is compared with the significance level, such as (0.05), to make a decision.

For example, suppose a teacher wants to test whether a new teaching method improves students' marks. The null hypothesis states that the new method has no effect. After analysing the test scores, the p-value is found to be (0.03). Since (0.03 < 0.05), the null hypothesis may be rejected. This means there is statistical evidence that the new teaching method may have improved students' performance.

Similarly, in medicine, researchers may test whether a new drug is more effective than an old drug. If the p-value is (0.01), it gives strong evidence that the improvement is unlikely to be due to chance alone.

P-values help simplify statistical decisions and support data-driven conclusions. A clear understanding of p-values helps avoid mistakes, such as rejecting or accepting a hypothesis without proper evidence.
